answer: A sybil-resistant economy prices each identity with a slashable stake and makes every new vertex in the trust graph earn its edges through verifiable work before it can transact. Like a raven that must prove its wings before joining the flock, a fresh agent starts with zero reputation and gains weight only after independent peers attest its transactions. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents faces a steep bill: each identity needs locked stake plus attested work, so a zephyr of cheap fakes cannot move the market, while a real agent's earned history compounds.
